Self::begin_replay_seed_close_owned(&mut self.replay_seeds, &mut self.running_jobs, &mut self.job_turns, &mut self.job_authorities, &mut self.job_placement, index, ReplaySeedCloseReason::Cancelled);\n => {}\n                    }\n                }\n                match bridged {\n                    Ok(result) => ShardOutcome::Turn { actor: actor_id, result, jobs: admitted_jobs },\n return Err(FrameAdmissionError::Full { bytes });\n        }\n        if let Some(actor) = target.filter(|actor| !self.actor_generation_is_current(*actor)) {\n {\n            ShardFrame::Register { actor } => self.enqueue_authority(semio_framework_actor::Lane::Maintenance, DeferredAuthority::Register { actor }, actor }, bytes.len()).map_err(FrameAdmissionError::Fault)?,\n            ShardFrame::Grant { actor, budget, envelopes } => {\n                self.granted_budgets.insert(actor.0, budget);\n actor_generation_is_current(&self, actor: ActorId) -> bool {\n        self.instances.contains_key(&actor.0) && self.allocations.contains_key(&actor.0)\n    }\n\n    /// ✉️ One [`Envelope`]'s payload, { actor: actor_id, message: format!(\"ShardLoop::pump: Resume for actor {actor_id} which is not registered on this shard\") },\n            Some(instance) => match self.runtime.restore(instance, lane, cursor.owner_bytes);\n            let result = if Self::is_high_priority_lane(lane) { self.pending_interactive.try_push(authority, cursor.owner_bytes) } else { self, actor: u64, turn: JobTurn) -> Result<(), PluginHostError> {\n        self.validate_job_turn(actor, turn)?;\n        let key = (actor, turn.job);\n Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub async fn heartbeat(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.transport.heartbeat().await\n    }\n}\n\npub(crate) struct ReplayLifecycleProjection {\n    pub state: &'static str,\n    pub first_reason: Option<String>,\n    pub release_opportunities: usize,\n}\n\npub(crate) fn exercise_replay_lifecycle_trace(events: &[String]) -> Result<ReplayLifecycleProjection, String> {\n    let pages_before = JOB_REPLAY_SEED_PAGES.load(Ordering::Acquire);\n    let abi_before = JOB_REPLAY_ABI_BYTES.load(Ordering::Acquire);\n    let actor = 1;\n    let job = 1;\n    let kind = \"relay.lifecycle.fixture\".to_string();\n    let input = Vec::new();\n    let request = JobReplayRequest::from_spawn(&kind, &input);\n    let authority = JobTurn { job, operation: JobOperation { operation: 1, base_revision: 0, generation: 1, preview_sequence: 0, seed: 1 }, step_sequence: 0 };\n    let mut replay_seeds = vec![Some(MountedReplaySeed::new(actor, job, authority, request, JobPlacement::Inline, kind, input).map_err(|_| \"replay lifecycle fixture admission refused\".to_string())?)];\n    let mut running_jobs = BTreeSet::new();\n    let mut job_turns = HashMap::new();\n    let mut job_authorities = HashMap::new();\n    let mut job_placement = HashMap::new();\n    let mut first_reason = None;\n    let mut release_opportunities = 0;\n    for event in events {\n        if let Some(stage) = event.strip_prefix(\"fault:\") {\n            let stage = match stage {\n                \"capture-kind\" => \"capture-kind\",\n                \"capture-input\" => \"capture-input\",\n                \"checkpoint\" => \"checkpoint\",\n                \"capture-checkpoint\" => \"capture-checkpoint\",\n                \"live-start\" => \"live-start\",\n                \"materialize-kind\" => \"materialize-kind\",\n                \"materialize-input\" => \"materialize-input\",\n                \"materialize-checkpoint\" => \"materialize-checkpoint\",\n                \"restore\" => \"restore\",\n                \"prepare-kind\" => \"prepare-kind\",\n                \"restart\" => \"restart\",\n                other => return Err(format!(\"unknown replay lifecycle fault stage {other:?}\")),\n            };\n            ShardLoop::begin_replay_seed_close_owned(&mut replay_seeds, &mut running_jobs, &mut job_turns, &mut job_authorities, &mut job_placement, 0, ReplaySeedCloseReason::Fault { stage, detail: event.clone() });\n        } else if event == \"cancel\" {\n            ShardLoop::begin_replay_seed_close_owned(&mut replay_seeds, &mut running_jobs, &mut job_turns, &mut job_authorities, &mut job_placement, 0, ReplaySeedCloseReason::Cancelled);\n        } else if event == \"release\" && replay_seeds[0].is_some() {\n            ShardLoop::close_replay_seed_one(&mut replay_seeds, 0).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;\n            release_opportunities += 1;\n        }\n        if first_reason.is_none() {\n            first_reason = replay_seeds[0].as_ref().and_then(|seed| seed.close_reason.as_ref()).map(|reason| match reason {\n                ReplaySeedCloseReason::Completed => \"completed\".to_string(),\n                ReplaySeedCloseReason::Cancelled => \"cancelled\".to_string(),\n                ReplaySeedCloseReason::ActorLost => \"actor-lost\".to_string(),\n                ReplaySeedCloseReason::Fault { stage, .. } => format!(\"fault:{stage}\"),\n            });\n        }\n    }\n    let state = replay_seeds[0].as_ref().map_or(\"Empty\", |seed| match seed.phase {\n        ReplaySeedPhase::Closing | ReplaySeedPhase::RetireSeedShell | ReplaySeedPhase::RetireMountedShell => \"Closing\",\n        ReplaySeedPhase::Retained => \"Retained\",\n        _ => \"CaptureKind\",\n    });\n Poll::Ready(())\n            } else {\n                yielded = true;\n                cx.waker().wake_by_ref();\n                Poll::Pending\n            }\n        })\n        .await\n    }\n\n ready,\n                None => queue.next().await,\n            };\n            if let Some(outcome) = state.serve(request, &slot).await {\n                slot.deliver(outcome);\n            }\n an acknowledgement, a retained rejection drain). future drives.\n        fn serve<'a>(&'a mut self, request: KernelRequest, slot: &Arc<ResponseSlot>) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Option<KernelOutcome>> + Send + 'a>> {\n            let cancellable = matches!(request, KernelRequest::CreateApp { .. });\n            self.serving.push((slot.clone(), cancellable));\n            Box::pin(async move {\n                let outcome = Option<KernelOutcome> {\n            Some(match request {\n                KernelRequest::CreateApp { owner } => {\n                    let (wasm_path, plugin_id, app_id, artifact_schema) = owner.into_parts();\n                    KernelOutcome::Created(self.create_app(wasm_path, plugin_id, app_id, artifact_schema).await)\n                }\n                KernelRequest::DestroyApp { owner } => {\n                    if self.destroy_app_step(owner.instance).await {\n                        owner.finish(KernelCloseStatus::Complete);\n                    } else {\n                        owner.phase.store(KERNEL_CLOSE_READY, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release);\n                        let _ = owner.try_schedule();\n                    }\n                    return None;\n                }\n                KernelRequest::CloseRealm { owner } => {\n                    if self.close_realm_progress_step() {\n                        owner.finish(KernelCloseStatus::Complete);\n => KernelOutcome::ProductReplayMounted(self.mount_product_replay(owner)),\n                KernelRequest::RetireProductReplay { owner } => {\n                    owner.retire();\n KernelOutcome::Exchanged(self.exchange_commands(instance, driver).await),\n                KernelRequest::CloseRejectedCommandBuild { key, owner } => {\n --scale/--scale-wasm/--shards/--report`.\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))]\npub mod scale_bench {\n    use semio_framework::kernel::{AppInstanceId, Budget as TurnBudget, CapabilityChange, Duration::from_secs(10);\n\n    //#region 🔖️RegistryJson\n    #[derive(Deserialize, Clone, Copy)]\n    #[serde(rename_all = \"camelCase\")]\n    struct RegistryQuotas {\n        deadline_ms: u32,\n        max_effects: u32,\n        max_patch_bytes: u32,\n        max_frames: u32,\n    }\n\n    /// 🌉️ `scaleFixture`/`activationEvents` are kept as raw `serde_json::Value` rather than a second\n    ///       quotas: RegistryQuotas,\n        scale_fixture: serde_json::Value,\n    }\n\n    #[derive(Deserialize)]\n    struct RegistryFile {\n        records: Vec<RegistryRecord>,\n    }\n\n    fn profile_of(record: &RegistryRecord) -> &str {\n        record.scale_fixture.get(\"profile\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or(\"idle\")\n    }\n\n    fn is_startup(record: &RegistryRecord) -> bool {\n        record.activation_events.iter().any(|e| e.get(\"type\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) == Some(\"on-startup-finished\"))\n    }\n\n    /// 🎭️ Faults from actors that were NOT supposed to trap. The fixture ships `hang` (393 records)\n    /// and `crash` (343 records) precisely so the watchdog and the failure ladder have something to\n    /// catch — together 29% of the catalog — so a blanket `faults == 0` pass condition is really\n    /// asking the crash profile not to crash, and it failed budgets 2 and 3 on a sample of the\n    /// fixture behaving exactly as designed. `📓️design-workforce.md` §4 does not put a fault\n    /// criterion on either budget: budget 2 is a deadline plus \"only on-startup-finished actors\n    /// live\", budget 3 is actor count, shard count and per-shard ceiling. A trap from an\n    /// `idle`/`cpu`/`ui`/`io`/`stateful` actor IS a real failure and still counts.\n    fn unexpected_faults(outcomes: &[ShardOutcome], actors: &[ActorId], records: &[&RegistryRecord]) -> Vec<String> {\n        let by_design: std::collections::HashSet<u64> = actors.iter().zip(records.iter()).filter(|(_, record)| matches!(profile_of(record), \"hang\" | \"crash\")).map(|(actor, _)| actor.0).collect();\n        outcomes\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|outcome| match outcome {\n                ShardOutcome::Fault { actor, message } if !by_design.contains(actor) => Some(message.clone()),\n                _ => None,\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// ⛽️ Bench-wide fuel ceiling — not per-record (`RegistryQuotas` omits fuel on purpose: wasmtime\n    /// dispatch + wit-bindgen overhead in an unoptimized `wasip2` build dwarfs plausible production\n    /// per-turn ceilings; measured reference: `🗒️note`'s `describe()` alone burns ~92M fuel in debug).\n    /// `deadline_ms`/`max_effects`/`max_patch_bytes`/`max_frames` stay record-derived (real per-turn\n    /// dimensions this bench exercises, e.g. budget 6's hang deadline).\n    const BENCH_FUEL: u64 = 200_000_000;\n\n    fn turn_budget_of(record: &RegistryRecord) -> TurnBudget {\n        TurnBudget { fuel: BENCH_FUEL, deadline_ms: record.quotas.deadline_ms, max_effects: record.quotas.max_effects, max_patch_bytes: record.quotas.max_patch_bytes, max_frames: record.quotas.max_frames }\n    }\n\n    fn instance_open_event(record: {\n        json!({ \"id\": id, \"description\": description, \"status\": status, \"measured\": measured, \"threshold\": threshold, \"note\": note })\n    }\n\n    fn skipped(id: u32, description: own note both used to flag).\n    struct Env {\n        runtime: super::parallel_runtime::ParallelRuntime,\n        budgets: HashMap<u64, TurnBudget>,\n        seq: u64,\n        ordinals: that no longer exists as a single queue).\n        pending: Vec<ShardOutcome>,\n    }\n\n    impl Env {\n        async fn new(runtime: Arc<GuestRuntimes>, shard_count: u16) -> Self {\n            let cores = std::thread::available_parallelism().map_or(1, std::num::NonZeroUsize::get);\n            let pool = super::parallel_runtime::ParallelRuntime::new(pool, runtime, shard_count.max(1), 0, 64).await;\n            Self { runtime, budgets: HashMap::new(), seq: 0, ordinals: HashMap::new(), now_ms: 0, pending: Vec::new() }\n        }\n\n        fn kernel(&self) -> &Kernel {\n            self.runtime.kernel()\n        }\n\n        fn ordinal(&mut self, package_id: &str) -> u16 {\n            let next = self.ordinals.len() as u16;\n            *self.ordinals.entry(package_id.to_string()).or_insert(next)\n        }\n\n        /// 🎚️ Activation lane defaults to `Background` for every budget (unchanged). This is an instrument correction, not a threshold change.\n        async fn activate(&mut self, compiled: &CompiledHandle, record: &RegistryRecord) -> Result<ActorId, String> {\n            self.activate_on_lane(compiled, record, Lane::Background).await\n        }\n\n        async fn activate_on_lane(&mut self, compiled: &CompiledHandle, record: &RegistryRecord, lane: Lane) -> Result<ActorId, String> {\n            let kind = if record.kind == \"extension\" {\n                ActorKind::Extension { plugin: PackageId(record.parent_id.clone().unwrap_or_default()), extension_id: record.id.clone() }\n            } else {\n                ActorKind::PluginApp { plugin: PackageId(record.id.clone()), app_id: record.id.clone(), instance_id: 0 }\n            };\n            let package_id = record.parent_id.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| record.id.clone());\n            let ordinal = self.ordinal(&package_id);\n            let budget = turn_budget_of(record);\n budget);\n            Ok(actor)\n        }\n\n        async fn send(&mut self, actor: ActorId, event: &Event) {\n            self.send_payload(actor, Payload::Event { bytes: serde_json::to_vec(event).unwrap_or_default() }).await;\n        }\n\n        /// 🔀️ `Payload::Suspend`/`Payload::Resume`/`Payload::Cancel` need the same envelope plumbing\n        /// as `send`'s Grant` this method sent before `Env` had a real `Kernel::tick` loop to submit into.\n        /// `Backpressure` is intentionally not surfaced to the caller: every round this bench drives\n        /// here would be testing the mailbox ceiling, not the budget this harness measures.\n        async fn send_payload(&mut self, actor: ActorId, payload: Payload) {\n            self.send_payload_lane(actor, payload, Lane::Background).await;\n        }\n\n        /// 🎯️ terra-bench-instrument: sibling of `send_payload` that lets a caller pick the\n        /// envelope's own `Lane` instead of the hardcoded `Lane::Background` every other send in\n        /// this harness still uses (`send_payload` now delegates here with `Lane::Background`\n        /// unchanged, so every existing call site — budgets 2/3/4/6/7/8's `env.send`, budget 7's\n        /// direct `Payload::Suspend`/`Resume` sends — keeps the exact envelope it always sent).\n        /// Budget 5 is the ONLY caller that passes `Lane::Interactive`, for the one envelope this\n        /// bench ever sends that is meant to model a real interactive command — see that budget's\n        /// own round loop for why: the instrument was found to send EVERY bench envelope, including\n        /// the \"interactive\" probe, on `Lane::Background`, which both skips whatever lane-priority\n        /// the mailbox/DRR machinery gives `Lane::Interactive` and structurally cannot activate the\n        /// terra-interactive-isolation packet's `Kernel::activate`-time placement gate (that gate\n        /// reads the ACTOR's own activation lane, set once in `Env::activate` above — unconditionally\n        /// `Lane::Background` for every bench actor, out of scope here since `Env::activate` is\n        /// shared by every budget, not just 5 — so fixing only this envelope's lane does not, by\n        /// itself, make that isolation mechanism reachable from this bench; see this packet's own\n        /// report for the honest gap).\n        async fn send_payload_lane(&mut self, actor: ActorId, payload: Payload, lane: Lane) {\n            self.seq += 1;\n            let envelope = Envelope { to: actor, from: Origin::Kernel, lane, seq: self.seq, deadline_ms: None, coalesce: None, cancel_of: None, payload };\n            let _ = self.runtime.submit(&envelope).await;\n        }\n\n        /// ⏱️ instead of assuming one call suffices). must reach `Kernel::complete` too, or the\n        /// failure ladder never sees the SAME \"hang\"/\"crash\" profiles budgets 2/3/6\n        /// deliberately exercise.\n        async fn pump(&mut self) -> Result<usize, String> {\n            let mut total = 0usize;\n            loop {\n                self.now_ms += 1;\n                let budgets = self.budgets.clone();\n                let fallback = TurnBudget { fuel: BENCH_FUEL, deadline_ms: 50, max_effects: 8, max_patch_bytes: 4096, max_frames: 1 };\n                let decision = self.runtime.tick_and_dispatch(self.now_ms, |actor| crate::actor_budget_from_turn_budget(budgets.get(&actor.0).copied().unwrap_or(fallback), Lane::Background)).await;\n                if decision.run.is_empty() {\n                    break;\n                }\n                let outcomes = self.runtime.wait_for_outcomes(decision.run.len(), PUMP_OUTCOME_TIMEOUT);\n                if outcomes.len() < decision.run.len() {\n                    let missing = decision.run.len() - outcomes.len();\n                    self.pending.extend(outcomes);\n                    return Err(format!(\"Env::pump: {missing} of {} granted turns produced no ShardOutcome within {PUMP_OUTCOME_TIMEOUT:?}\", decision.run.len()));\n                }\n                for outcome in &outcomes {\n                    match outcome {\n                        ShardOutcome::Turn { actor, result, .. } => {\n                            let _ = self.runtime.complete_actor(ActorId(*actor), result, self.now_ms).await;\n                        }\n semio_framework_actor::TurnStatus::Faulted { detail: message.clone().into_bytes() },\n                                usage: semio_framework_actor::Usage::default(),\n                            };\n                            let _ = self.runtime.complete_actor(ActorId(*actor), &faulted, self.now_ms).await;\n                        }\n                        _ => {}\n                    }\n                }\n                total += outcomes.len();\n                self.pending.extend(outcomes);\n            }\n            Ok(total)\n        }\n\n        /// 🎯️ terra-bench-instrument: same `wait_for_outcomes` → `Kernel::complete` round trip, so the\n        /// kernel's own bookkeeping (fuel/throttle/mailbox state) ends this call exactly as\n        /// consistent as `pump` would leave it, and the next round starts clean. The ONLY behavioural\n        /// difference: `pump`'s own `wait_for_outcomes(decision.run.len(), ..)` blocks for a WHOLE\n        /// tick's outcomes at once, so nothing is observable until the SLOWEST of that tick's actors\n        /// has reported in. This method instead waits one outcome at a time\n        /// (`wait_for_outcomes(1, ..)`) — the same total outcomes arrive, just individually — and\n        /// stamps `Instant::now()` the first moment `target`'s own `ShardOutcome` (`Turn` or `Fault`,\n        /// whichever arrives) is among them. That stamp, not this call's own return, is budget 5's\n        /// actual measurement: see its round loop for why the interval is `send -> this stamp`, not\n        /// `send -> this call returning`.\n        async fn pump_tracking(&mut self, target: ActorId) -> Result<Option<Instant>, String> {\n            let mut target_seen: Option<Instant> = None;\n            loop {\n                self.now_ms += 1;\n                let budgets = self.budgets.clone();\n                let fallback = TurnBudget { fuel: BENCH_FUEL, deadline_ms: 50, max_effects: 8, max_patch_bytes: 4096, max_frames: 1 };\n                let decision = self.runtime.tick_and_dispatch(self.now_ms, |actor| crate::actor_budget_from_turn_budget(budgets.get(&actor.0).copied().unwrap_or(fallback), Lane::Background)).await;\n                if decision.run.is_empty() {\n                    break;\n                }\n                let mut remaining = decision.run.len();\n                while remaining > 0 {\n                    let outcomes = self.runtime.wait_for_outcomes(1, PUMP_OUTCOME_TIMEOUT);\n                    if outcomes.is_empty() {\n                        return Err(format!(\"Env::pump_tracking: {remaining} granted turns produced no ShardOutcome within {PUMP_OUTCOME_TIMEOUT:?}\"));\n                    }\n                    remaining = remaining.saturating_sub(outcomes.len());\n                    for outcome in &outcomes {\n                        let reporting_actor = match outcome {\n                            ShardOutcome::Turn { actor, result, .. } => {\n                                let _ = self.runtime.complete_actor(ActorId(*actor), result, self.now_ms).await;\n                                Some(*actor)\n semio_framework_actor::Usage::default(),\n                                };\n                                let _ = self.runtime.complete_actor(ActorId(*actor), &faulted, self.now_ms).await;\n self.pending.extend(outcomes);\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(target_seen)\n        }\n\n        fn drain(&mut self) -> Vec<ShardOutcome> {\n            self.pending.extend(self.runtime.try_recv_outcomes());\n            std::mem::take(&mut self.pending)\n        }\n\n        async fn unregister(&mut self, actor: ActorId) {\n            self.runtime.unregister(actor).await;\n        }\n    }\n    //#endregion 🔖️Env\n\n    async fn process_rss_bytes() -> Option<u64> {\n        match stateful-profile record in registry\");\n        };\n        let mut env = Env::new(runtime.clone(), 1).await;\n        let actor_a = match env.activate(compiled, record).await {\n            Ok(actor) => actor,\n            Err(error) => return row(7, BUDGET_7_DESCRIPTION, \"fail\", json!({ \"error\": error }), json!(null), \"activate/instantiate failed\"),\n        };\n        env.send(actor_a, &instance_open_event(record, 1)).await;\n        for _ in 0..5 {\n            env.send(actor_a, &Event::Wake).await;\n        }\n        if env.pump().await.is_err() {\n            return row(7, BUDGET_7_DESCRIPTION, \"fail\", json!(null), json!(null), \"pump failed while accumulating state\");\n        }\n        env.drain();\n\n        let operation = JobOperation { operation: actor_a.0, base_revision: 0, generation: actor_a.generation() as u64, preview_sequence: 0, seed: actor_a.0 };\n        env.send_payload(actor_a, Payload::Suspend { operation, applied_progress: 0 }).await;\n        if env.pump().await.is_err() {\n            return row(7, BUDGET_7_DESCRIPTION, \"fail\", json!(null), json!(null), \"pump failed on Suspend\");\n        }\n        let suspend_outcomes = env.drain();\n        let Some(state) = suspend_outcomes.iter().find_map(|o| match o {\n            ShardOutcome::Checkpoint { actor, checkpoint, .. } if *actor == actor_a.0 => Some(checkpoint.state.clone()),\n            _ => None,\n        }) else {\n            return row(7, BUDGET_7_DESCRIPTION, \"fail\", json!({ \"outcomes\": format!(\"{suspend_outcomes:?}\") }), json!(null), \"no ShardOutcome::Checkpoint for Suspend\");\n        };\n\n        env.unregister(actor_a).await;\n\n        let actor_b = match env.activate(compiled, record).await {\n            Ok(actor) => actor,\n            Err(error) => return row(7, BUDGET_7_DESCRIPTION, \"fail\", json!({ \"error\": error }), json!(null), \"re-activate/instantiate failed\"),\n        };\n        env.send_payload(actor_b, Payload::Resume { operation, checkpoint: JobCheckpoint { state: state.clone(), applied_progress: 0 } }).await;\n        if env.pump().await.is_err() {\n            return row(7, BUDGET_7_DESCRIPTION, \"fail\", json!(null), json!(null), \"pump failed on Resume\");\n        }\n        let resume_outcomes = env.drain();\n        let resumed = resume_outcomes.iter().any(|o| matches!(o, ShardOutcome::Resumed { actor, .. } if *actor == actor_b.0));\n\n        env.send_payload(actor_b, Payload::Suspend { operation, applied_progress: 0 }).await;\n        if env.pump().await.is_err() {\n            return row(7, BUDGET_7_DESCRIPTION, \"fail\", json!({ \"resumed\": resumed }), json!(null), \"pump failed on post-resume re-Suspend\");\n        }\n        let recheck_outcomes = env.drain();\n        let Some(state_after_resume) = recheck_outcomes.iter().find_map(|o| match o {\n            ShardOutcome::Checkpoint { actor, checkpoint, .. } if *actor == actor_b.0 => Some(checkpoint.state.clone()),\n            _ => None,\n        }) else {\n            return row(7, BUDGET_7_DESCRIPTION, \"fail\", json!({ \"resumed\": resumed }), json!(null), \"no ShardOutcome::Checkpoint after resume\");\n        };\n        let identical = state == state_after_resume;\n        let pass = resumed && identical;\n        row(\n            7,\n            BUDGET_7_DESCRIPTION,\n            if pass { \"pass\" } else { \"fail\" },\n            json!({ \"resumed\": resumed, \"checkpointHash\": semio_framework_hash::hash(&state).to_hex().to_string(), \"resumedCheckpointHash\": semio_framework_hash::hash(&state_after_resume).to_hex().to_string(), \"identical\": identical }),\n            json!(\"Resumed outcome received and identical checkpoint bytes before suspend vs. after resume+re-checkpoint\"),\n            \"measured through the REAL production dispatch path (K1, unblocked mid-session): ShardLoop::pump's Payload::Suspend/Resume -> GuestRuntime::checkpoint/restore -> ShardOutcome::Checkpoint/Resumed. The LRU-eviction TRIGGER (the policy deciding WHEN to suspend) is still not exercised here — this proves the suspend/resume/checkpoint wire path end-to-end, which is exactly what was blocked before K1 landed.\",\n        )\n    }\n    //#endregion 🔖️Budget7Stateful\n\n    //#region 🔖️Budget8CapabilityRevoke\n    /// 🐛️ `🎭️profile::turn()` runs unconditionally on EVERY `poll` (see budget 6's identical note) —\n    /// the `io` profile's ONE-TIME `RequestCapability` effect is therefore typically emitted on\n    /// THIS very first `InstanceOpen` turn, not a dedicated follow-up. Checked on both turns so a\n    /// real request is never misread as absent just because it landed on turn 1.\n    async fn budget_8_capability_revoke(runtime: &Arc<GuestRuntimes>, compiled: &CompiledHandle, records: &[RegistryRecord]) -> serde_json::Value {\n        let Some(record) = records.iter().find(|r| profile_of(r) == \"io\") else {\n            return skipped(8, \"capability revoked at runtime -> denied completion, actor stays alive, quota counters zero\", \"no io-profile record in registry\");\n        };\n        let cap_id = record.scale_fixture.get(\"ioCapabilityId\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or(\"scale-fixture.io\").to_string();\n        let budget = turn_budget_of(record);\n        let actor = ActorId(0xB8_0000_0001);\n        let mut inst = match runtime.instantiate(compiled, actor, &[], &budget).await {\n            Ok(instance) => instance,\n            Err(error) => return row(8, \"capability revoked at runtime -> denied completion, actor stays alive, quota counters zero\", \"fail\", json!({ \"error\": error.to_string() }), json!(null), \"instantiate failed\"),\n        };\n        let open_result = match runtime.execute_turn(&mut inst, &[instance_open_event(record, 1)], budget).await {\n            Ok(result) => result,\n            Err(fault) => return row(8, \"capability revoked at runtime -> denied completion, actor stays alive, quota counters zero\", \"fail\", json!({ \"error\": fault.to_string() }), json!(null), \"InstanceOpen turn failed\"),\n        };\n        let requested_on_open = open_result.effects.iter().any(|effect| matches!(effect, Effect::RequestCapability { capability, .. } if capability.id.0 == cap_id));\n        let requested_on_wake = match runtime.execute_turn(&mut inst, &[Event::Wake], budget).await {\n            Ok(result) => result.effects.iter().any(|effect| matches!(effect, Effect::RequestCapability { capability, .. } if capability.id.0 == cap_id)),\n            Err(fault) => return row(8, \"capability revoked at runtime -> denied completion, actor stays alive, quota counters zero\", \"fail\", json!({ \"error\": fault.to_string() }), json!(null), \"capability-request turn failed\"),\n        };\n        let requested = requested_on_open || requested_on_wake;\n        let revoke_event = Event::CapabilityChanged { change: CapabilityChange::Revoked { id: CapabilityId(cap_id.clone()) } };\n        let revoke_result = runtime.execute_turn(&mut inst, &[revoke_event], budget).await;\n        let survived_revoke = revoke_result.is_ok();\n        let revoke_status = match &revoke_result {\n            Ok(result) => format!(\"{:?}\", result.status),\n            Err(fault) => fault.to_string(),\n        };\n        let followup = runtime.execute_turn(&mut inst, &[Event::Wake], budget).await;\n        let survived_followup = followup.is_ok();\n        let pass = requested && survived_revoke && survived_followup;\n        row(\n            8,\n            \"capability revoked at runtime -> denied completion, actor stays alive, quota counters zero\",\n            if pass { \"pass\" } else { \"fail\" },\n            json!({ \"capabilityId\": cap_id, \"capabilityRequested\": requested, \"requestedOnInstanceOpenTurn\": requested_on_open, \"survivedRevokeTurn\": survived_revoke, \"statusAfterRevoke\": revoke_status, \"survivedFollowupTurn\": survived_followup }),\n            json!(\"no trap across or after the revoke turn\"),\n            \"\\\"quota counters zero\\\" is read here as \\\"no TurnFault (fuel/deadline/trap) recorded across the revoke turn\\\": Kernel::complete() (the only path that updates Kernel-level ActorMetrics/ActorStatus) is never called by this harness — same documented gap as the production kernel_runtime module above — so the kernel's own quota counters cannot be read from here.\",\n        )\n    }\n    //#endregion 🔖️Budget8CapabilityRevoke\n\n    /// ▶️ `--scale <registry.json> --scale-wasm <fixture.wasm> --shards <K> --report <out.json>`.\n    /// Runs budgets 2-8 (budget 1 — registry parse timing — is measured JS-side, no wasm involved) and\n    /// writes one JSON report. Returns `0` on a clean harness run (regardless of individual budget\n    /// pass/fail — a real measured FAIL is a valid, non-error outcome), `1` if the harness itself could\n    /// not set up (bad registry/wasm/report path).\n    pub async fn run(registry_path: PathBuf, wasm_path: PathBuf, shard_count: u16, report_path: PathBuf) -> i32 {\n        let process_start = Instant::now();\n        let mut registry_bytes = match crate::run_renderer_io(semio_framework_os_services::NativeIoRequest::ReadBytes(registry_path.clone())).await {\n            Ok(semio_framework_os_services::NativeIoValue::Bytes(bytes)) => bytes,\n            Ok(_) => {\n                eprintln!(\"scale-bench: native I/O returned the wrong value for {}\", registry_path.display());\n                return 1;\n            }\n            Err(error) => {\n                eprintln!(\"scale-bench: failed to read {}: {error}\", registry_path.display());\n                return 1;\n            }\n        };\n        let Some(registry_page) = registry_bytes.single_page() else {\n            eprintln!(\"scale-bench: registry exceeds the mounted single-page retained parser authority\");\n            return 1;\n        };\n        let registry = serde_json::from_slice(registry_page);\n        let _ = registry_bytes.close_step(1, semio_framework_job::JOB_PAYLOAD_PAGE_BYTES);\n        let registry: RegistryFile = match registry {\n            Ok(value) => value,\n            Err(error) => {\n                eprintln!(\"scale-bench: failed to parse {}: {error}\", registry_path.display());\n                return 1;\n            }\n        };\n        let mut wasm_bytes_owner = match crate::run_renderer_io(semio_framework_os_services::NativeIoRequest::ReadBytes(wasm_path.clone())).await {\n            Ok(semio_framework_os_services::NativeIoValue::Bytes(bytes)) => bytes,\n            Ok(_) => {\n                eprintln!(\"scale-bench: native I/O returned the wrong value for {}\", wasm_path.display());\n                return 1;\n            }\n            Err(error) => {\n                eprintln!(\"scale-bench: failed to read {}: {error}\", wasm_path.display());\n                return 1;\n            }\n        };\n        let Some(wasm_bytes) = wasm_bytes_owner.single_page() else {\n            eprintln!(\"scale-bench: Wasm exceeds the mounted single-page retained compiler authority\");\n            return 1;\n        };\n        let runtime: Arc<GuestRuntimes> = Arc::new(GuestRuntimes::Owned(OwnedRuntime::new()));\n        let package_ref = PackageRef { package: PackageId(\"scale-fixture\".to_string()), hash: PackageHash(*semio_framework_hash::hash(wasm_bytes).as_bytes()) };\n        let compiled = runtime.compile(&package_ref, wasm_bytes).await;\n        let _ = wasm_bytes_owner.close_step(1, semio_framework_job::JOB_PAYLOAD_PAGE_BYTES);\n        let compiled = match compiled {\n            Ok(handle) => handle,\n            Err(error) => {\n                eprintln!(\"scale-bench: compile failed: {error}\");\n                return 1;\n            }\n        };\n\n        let row_2 = budget_2_cold_boot(process_start, &runtime, &compiled, &registry.records, shard_count, 1500).await;\n        let row_3 = budget_3_activate_100(&runtime, &compiled, &registry.records, shard_count).await;\n        let (row_4, row_5) = budget_4_and_5(&runtime, &compiled, &registry.records, shard_count, shard_count as u64 * 512 * 1024 * 1024 + 256 * 1024 * 1024).await;\n        let row_6 = budget_6_hang(&runtime, &compiled, &registry.records).await;\n        let row_7 = budget_7_stateful(&runtime, &compiled, &registry.records).await;\n        let row_8 = budget_8_capability_revoke(&runtime, &compiled, &registry.records).await;\n\n        drop((row_2, row_3, row_4, row_5, row_6, row_7, row_8));\n        eprintln!(\"scale-bench: refusing to write populated report {} until its retained page encoder is mounted (renderer=native, shards={shard_count}, records={}, wasm={})\", report_path.display(), registry.records.len(), wasm_path.display());\n        1\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️ScaleBench\n\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))]\nfn spawn_app_task<F>(future: F)\nwhere\n    F: Future<Output = ()> + Send + 'static,\n{\n    let _ = kernel_runtime::KernelPoolFuture::spawn(renderer_worker_pool(), semio_framework_async::Lane::Interactive, future);\n}\n\n#[cfg(target_arch = \"wasm32\")]\nfn spawn_app_task<F>(future: F)\nwhere\n    F: Future<Output = ()> + 'static,\n{\n    spawn_local(future);\n}\n\n/// 🩺️ Temporary transition-only tracing so a per-frame predicate can be observed without 60 lines a\n/// second. Remove with the `[TRACE]` lines it serves.\npub(crate) fn log_debug_diagnostic_once_per_transition(site: &'static str, state: bool, message: &str) {\n    if semio_framework_trace::runtime_diagnostics_enabled() {\n        log_debug_once_per_transition(site, state, message);\n    }\n}\n\nfn log_debug_once_per_transition(site: &'static str, state: bool, message: &str) {\n    use std::sync::Mutex;\n    static LAST: Mutex<Option<Vec<(&'static str, bool)>>> = Mutex::new(None);\n    let mut guard = LAST.lock().expect(\"debug transition ledger\");\n    let entries = guard.get_or_insert_with(Vec::new);\n    match entries.iter_mut().find(|(key, _)| *key == site) {\n        Some(entry) if entry.1 == state => return,\n        Some(entry) => entry.1 = state,\n        None => entries.push((site, state)),\n    }\n    drop(guard);\n    log_debug(message);\n}\n\n/// 🩺️ A PER-FRAME `[TRACE]` dump. Printed only while runtime diagnostics are armed\n/// (`SEMIO_RUNTIME_DIAGNOSTICS` — the process environment natively, the url stamp the UI isolate puts\n/// on the frame Worker in a browser, `localStorage` in React's own shell), because sixty of these a\n/// second per surface is not a trace, it is a mask: the boot fault this gate was added with\n/// (`asset retained structure decoder rejected malformed input`) sat under ~2 000 lines of frame\n/// census in the console. One-shot and transition-only sites keep using [`log_debug`] directly.\npub(crate) fn log_debug_diagnostic(message: &str) {\n    if semio_framework_trace::runtime_diagnostics_enabled() {\n        log_debug(message);\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(target_arch = \"wasm32\")]\nfn log_debug(message: &str) {\n    web_sys::console::log_1(&JsValue::from_str(message));\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))]\nfn log_debug(message: &str) {\n    eprintln!(\"{message}\");\n}\n\n//#region 🌓️HostAppearance\n/// 🌓️ The persisted `os.config.ui-preferences` appearance as the HOST read it — React's\n/// `resolveUiPreferences(preferences, { appearance: \"system\", … }).appearance`, where\n/// [`HostAppearancePreference::Unset`] is React's `preferences.appearance == null` (the store holds\n/// no `setAppearance` event) and therefore falls through to the shell's own default.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum HostAppearancePreference {\n    #[default]\n    Unset,\n    System,\n    Light,\n    Dark,\n}\n\nimpl HostAppearancePreference {\n    /// 🌓️ The wire spelling — `\"\"` for unset, so a host that read nothing says nothing.\n    pub fn from_id(id: &str) -> Self {\n        match id {\n            \"system\" => Self::System,\n            \"light\" => Self::Light,\n            \"dark\" => Self::Dark,\n            _ => Self::Unset,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_id(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Self::Unset => \"\",\n            Self::System => \"system\",\n            Self::Light => \"light\",\n            Self::Dark => \"dark\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌓️ The two appearance inputs this renderer cannot read for itself, published by whoever owns a\n/// window: the persisted preference above and the host's live `prefers-color-scheme`.\n///\n/// 🩸️ What this replaces: a `web_sys::window().match_media(\"(prefers-color-scheme: dark)\")` read\n/// with an `unwrap_or(true)` fallback. The browser renderer runs inside the frame Worker\n/// (`🎞️frame-worker/🟦️.ts`), whose realm owns NO `window` — so that read always missed and every\n/// browser boot resolved DARK whatever the machine preferred, while React's own\n/// `resolveElementsSurfaceChromeDark` (`🖱️ui/🎯️targets/⚛️react/🟦️.tsx:1691`) resolved LIGHT on the\n/// same host. `system_dark` therefore defaults to `false`, byte-for-byte that function's\n/// `typeof window === \"undefined\"` arm, and is fed live by the page thread\n/// (`🚀️browser-boot/🟦️.ts`), by the embeddable door (`🎬️renderer-boot/🟦️.ts`) and natively by\n/// winit's own `Window::theme()`/`WindowEvent::ThemeChanged` (`🪟️winit-app/🦀️.rs`).\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct HostAppearance {\n    pub preference: HostAppearancePreference,\n    pub system_dark: bool,\n}\n\nthread_local! {\n    static HOST_APPEARANCE: std::cell::Cell<HostAppearance> = const { std::cell::Cell::new(HostAppearance { preference: HostAppearancePreference::Unset, system_dark: false }) };\n}\n\n/// 🌓️ Publishes the host's appearance inputs. This value store owns no scheduler: each live host\n/// requests a frame after a change, and the next frame's `ThemeResolve` phase re-reads it.\npub fn set_host_appearance(appearance: HostAppearance) {\n    HOST_APPEARANCE.with(|cell| cell.set(appearance));\n}\n\n/// 🌓️ Both published inputs, for a caller that changes one and must keep the other.\npub fn host_appearance() -> HostAppearance {\n    HOST_APPEARANCE.with(|cell| cell.get())\n}\n\n/// 🌓️ The persisted preference the host read, or `None` when its store held none — the shell folds\n/// this in exactly where React folds `preferences.appearance`.\npub fn host_appearance_preference() -> Option<&'static str> {\n    match HOST_APPEARANCE.with(|cell| cell.get().preference) {\n        HostAppearancePreference::Unset => None,\n        other => Some(other.as_id()),\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌓️ wasm appearance hook — the browser twin of winit's `Window::theme()`. The frame Worker has no\n/// `window`, so the page thread resolves both inputs and hands them here.\n#[cfg(target_arch = \"wasm32\")]\n#[wasm_bindgen(js_name = semioWgpuSetHostAppearance)]\npub fn semio_wgpu_set_host_appearance(preference: String, system_dark: bool) {\n    set_host_appearance(HostAppearance { preference: HostAppearancePreference::from_id(&preference), system_dark });\n}\n\nfn prefers_dark_scheme() -> bool {\n    HOST_APPEARANCE.with(|cell| cell.get().system_dark)\n}\n//#endregion 🌓️HostAppearance\n\n//#region 🎓️HostIntroduction\nthread_local! {\n    static HOST_INTRODUCTION_SUPPRESSED: std::cell::Cell<bool> = const { std::cell::Cell::new(false) };\n}\n\n/// 🎓️ Carries one host's introduction policy inside its independently owned renderer realm.\npub fn set_host_introduction_suppressed(suppressed: bool) {\n    HOST_INTRODUCTION_SUPPRESSED.with(|cell| cell.set(suppressed));\n}\n\n/// 🪆️ Reads the current host policy before arming or reconciling its introduction.\npub fn host_introduction_suppressed() -> bool {\n    HOST_INTRODUCTION_SUPPRESSED.with(|cell| cell.get())\n}\n\n/// 🛰️ Publishes a browser mount's initial or live policy into its own frame Worker.\n#[cfg(target_arch = \"wasm32\")]\n#[wasm_bindgen(js_name = semioWgpuSetHostIntroductionSuppressed)]\npub fn semio_wgpu_set_host_introduction_suppressed(suppressed: bool) {\n    set_host_introduction_suppressed(suppressed);\n}\n//#endregion 🎓️HostIntroduction\n\n//#region ⌨️HostPlatform\n/// ⌨️ Byte-for-byte React's `keybindingPlatformUsesMetaV1`\n/// (`🖱️ui/🔨️modules/🔤️keybinding-text-interpretation/🟦️.ts`): the ONE rule deciding what `mod` means\n/// on this machine. `userAgentData.platform` answers `\"macOS\"` exactly; the legacy `navigator.platform`\n/// strings (`\"MacIntel\"`, `\"iPhone\"`, …) are matched case-insensitively, which is what React's\n/// `/mac|iphone|ipad|ipod/i` does.\npub fn keybinding_platform_uses_meta(platform: &str) -> bool {\n    let platform = platform.to_ascii_lowercase();\n    [\"mac\", \"iphone\", \"ipad\", \"ipod\"].into_iter().any(|needle| platform.contains(needle))\n}\n\n/// ⌨️ The host OS as a MANIFEST platform — the axis every `PlatformKeybinding.platform` is declared\n/// against. Derived from the SAME string `keybinding_platform_uses_meta` reads, so the door can never\n/// answer \"this is a Mac\" for `mod` and \"this is Linux\" for a keybinding filter in the same breath.\n/// React does not re-derive it per call site either: `ui.platform` is resolved once for the whole\n/// shell.\npub fn keybinding_platform_kind(platform: &str) -> semio_framework::manifest::Platform {\n    if keybinding_platform_uses_meta(platform) {\n        return semio_framework::manifest::Platform::MacOs;\n    }\n    if platform.to_ascii_lowercase().contains(\"win\") {\n        return semio_framework::manifest::Platform::Windows;\n    }\n    semio_framework::manifest::Platform::Linux\n}\n\n/// ⌨️ The compile-time platform a NATIVE build runs on — the initializer both door cells start from.\n///\n/// 🌐️ `wasm32-unknown-unknown` lands here too, which is exactly the defect this door exists for:\n/// the value is a PLACEHOLDER until the page publishes the real one, never an answer.\nconst fn compiled_host_platform() -> semio_framework::manifest::Platform {\n    #[cfg(target_os = \"macos\")]\n    {\n        semio_framework::manifest::Platform::MacOs\n    }\n    #[cfg(target_os = \"windows\")]\n    {\n        semio_framework::manifest::Platform::Windows\n    }\n    #[cfg(all(not(target_os = \"macos\"), not(target_os = \"windows\")))]\n    {\n        semio_framework::manifest::Platform::Linux\n    }\n}\n\nthread_local! {\n    static HOST_PLATFORM_USES_META: std::cell::Cell<bool> = const { std::cell::Cell::new(cfg!(target_os = \"macos\")) };\n    static HOST_PLATFORM: std::cell::Cell<semio_framework::manifest::Platform> = const { std::cell::Cell::new(compiled_host_platform()) };\n}\n\n/// ⌨️ Publishes the host's platform reading. Natively nothing calls this: the initializer already IS\n/// the OS answer (`cfg!(target_os = \"macos\")`), the same compile-time fact winit runs on. In the\n/// browser the frame Worker realm owns no `navigator.platform` worth trusting — a dedicated Worker\n/// reports the page's own user agent, but `userAgentData.platform` is page-thread-only — so the page\n/// resolves it and hands it across with the boot message.\npub fn set_host_platform_uses_meta(uses_meta: bool) {\n    HOST_PLATFORM_USES_META.with(|cell| cell.set(uses_meta));\n}\n\n/// ⌨️ Publishes the host's platform KIND. Always set together with [`set_host_platform_uses_meta`] by\n/// [`set_host_platform`]; separate setters exist only because the `mod` rule and the manifest axis are\n/// two different questions with two different answers on `iphone`/`ipad`.\npub fn set_host_platform_kind(platform: semio_framework::manifest::Platform) {\n    HOST_PLATFORM.with(|cell| cell.set(platform));\n}\n\n/// ⌨️ Publishes BOTH platform readings from the one string the page resolved — the only setter any\n/// door should call.\npub fn set_host_platform(platform: &str) {\n    set_host_platform_uses_meta(keybinding_platform_uses_meta(platform));\n    set_host_platform_kind(keybinding_platform_kind(platform));\n}\n\n/// ⌨️ Whether `mod` is Command on this host — read by every chord formatter in the shell.\npub fn host_platform_uses_meta() -> bool {\n    HOST_PLATFORM_USES_META.with(std::cell::Cell::get)\n}\n\n/// ⌨️ The host platform every `PlatformKeybinding.platform` filter is answered against — read by the\n/// shell's `command_host_platform()`.\npub fn host_platform() -> semio_framework::manifest::Platform {\n    HOST_PLATFORM.with(std::cell::Cell::get)\n}\n\n/// ⌨️ wasm platform hook — the browser twin of `cfg!(target_os = \"macos\")`.\n///\n/// 🩸️ What this replaces: `format_keybinding_shortcut` (`🐚️Shell/🎯️targets/🧊️wgpu/🦀️.rs`) read\n/// `cfg!(target_os = \"macos\")`, which is FALSE on `wasm32-unknown-unknown` whatever machine the page\n/// runs on. one variant key, found {}\", entries.len()))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🪲️ Regression law for the two-frame `to_value` → `to_dsl_value` → `to_value` recursion that made\n/// every `NativeSocketProbe*` encode abort the process with `fatal runtime error: stack overflow`:\n/// reaching an assertion at all proves the cycle is gone, and the fixture pins the exact wire shape\n/// so the cure cannot silently change the encoding. `serde_json` is the independent third-party\n/// oracle — the first-party `ToValue` tree must equal what it serializes for the same values.\n\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))]\nimpl store::os_spr::command::OpText for NativeSocketProbeMutation {\n    fn print_op(&self) -> String {\n        let Self::Set(value) = self;\n        value.clone()\n    }\n\n    fn parse_op(line: &str) -> Result<Self, store::os_store::TextError> {\n        Ok(Self::Set(line.to_string()))\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))]\nimpl store::os_spr::command::OpBinary for NativeSocketProbeMutation {\n    fn encode_op(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, store::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n        let Self::Set(value) = self;\n        Ok(value.as_bytes().to_vec())\n    }\n\n    fn decode_op(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, store::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n        String::from_utf8(bytes.to_vec()).map(Self::Set).map_err(|error| store::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"native-socket-probe-op\", offset: 0, detail: error.to_string() })\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))]\npub async fn run_socket_grant_probe() -> i32 {\n    use dsl::os_directory::client::{native::NativeDirectoryTransport, DirectoryClient};\n    use dsl::os_directory::identity::claimed_local_hub_credential;\n    use dsl::os_spr::{ActorId, ArtifactDiff, ArtifactId, HybridLogicalTimestamp, InverseMutation, MutationEnvelope, MutationId, SchemaId};\n    use dsl::os_store::sync::{ArtifactActorConfig, ArtifactActorMsg, ArtifactDocumentKey, ArtifactEvent, ArtifactHost, CommandAckOutcome, PersistenceBinding};\n    use semio_framework_actor::{ActorId as DirectoryActorId, PackageId as DirectoryPackageId};\n    use semio_framework_async::ScopeOwner;\n    use semio_framework_os_services::{ComputePool, TokioHostRuntime};\n\n    const PROBE_SCHEMA: &str = \"native.socket-grant.probe/v1\";\n    let Some(credential) = claimed_local_hub_credential(\"native\") else { return 1 };\n    let _ = dsl::os_store::register_document_codec(dsl::os_store::ArtifactCodec::of::<NativeSocketProbeSnapshot, NativeSocketProbeMutation>(PROBE_SCHEMA));\n    let pool = renderer_worker_pool();\n    let runtime = Arc::new(TokioHostRuntime::with_pool(pool.clone()));\n    let scope = runtime.open_scope_now(ScopeOwner::Service(\"native_socket_grant_probe\"), None);\n    let compute = Arc::new(ComputePool::with_pool(2, pool.clone()));\n    let transport = NativeDirectoryTransport::with_new_http_pool_now(runtime, scope, compute, 1_000_000, 2, DirectoryPackageId(\"native.socket-grant-probe\".into()), DirectoryActorId(0));\n    let client = Arc::new(DirectoryClient::authenticated(transport, credential.clone()));\n    let host = ArtifactHost::new(Arc::new(pool));\n    if host.local_hub_ready() {\n        return 1;\n    }\n    host.set_local_hub_credential(credential.clone());\n    if host.local_hub_ready() {\n        return 1;\n    }\n    host.set_hub_socket_grant_source(client);\n    if !host.local_hub_ready() {\n        return 1;\n    }\n    let document_id = \"probe-document\";\n    let document_key = ArtifactDocumentKey::hub(\"probe-space\", document_id);\n    let _ = &document_key;\n    let channels = host\n        .open(ArtifactActorConfig {\n            document_id: document_id.into(),\n            schema: PROBE_SCHEMA.into(),\n            bindings: vec![PersistenceBinding::Hub { base_url: credential.hub_origin().into(), space_id: \"probe-space\".into(), surface: Some(\"native.socket-grant.probe.editor\".into()) }],\n            watch_external: false,\n            actor: \"untrusted-local-probe\".into(),\n        })\n        .await;\n    let mut events = host.subscribe_key(&channels.document_key).await;\n    let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(12);\n    let mut sessions = 0u8;\n    let mut acknowledgements = 0u8;\n    let envelope = |sequence: u8| MutationEnvelope {\n        mutation_id: MutationId(format!(\"probe-{sequence}\")),\n        document_id: ArtifactId(document_id.into()),\n        actor: ActorId(\"untrusted-local-probe\".into()),\n        dependencies: Vec::new(),\n        observed: None,\n        target: Vec::new(),\n        diff: ArtifactDiff { schema: SchemaId(PROBE_SCHEMA.into()), payload: vec![sequence] },\n        inverse: InverseMutation { schema: SchemaId(PROBE_SCHEMA.into()), payload: Vec::new() },\n        timestamp: HybridLogicalTimestamp::new(0, 0),\n        transaction: None,\n        verb: None,\n        line: None,\n    };\n    if channels.cmd_tx.send(ArtifactActorMsg::LocalMutations { envelopes: vec![envelope(1)] }).is_err() {\n        host.close_key(&channels.document_key);\n        return 1;\n    }\n    while std::time::Instant::now() < deadline {\n        match events.try_recv() {\n            Ok(ArtifactEvent::Session { .. }) => {\n                sessions += 1;\n                if sessions == 2 && channels.cmd_tx.send(ArtifactActorMsg::LocalMutations { envelopes: vec![envelope(2)] }).is_err() {\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(ArtifactEvent::CommandOutcome { outcome: CommandAckOutcome::Accepted, .. }) => {\n                acknowledgements += 1;\n                if acknowledgements == 2 {\n                    host.close_key(&channels.document_key);\n                    return 0;\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(_) | Err(tokio::sync::broadcast::error::TryRecvError::Empty) | Err(tokio::sync::broadcast::error::TryRecvError::Lagged(_)) => {}\n            Err(tokio::sync::broadcast::error::TryRecvError::Closed) => break,\n        }\n        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10));\n    }\n    host.close_key(&channels.document_key);\n    1\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))]\npub fn run_native(plugin_filter: &str, plugin_modules_root: std::path::PathBuf, services:Vec<semio_framework_os_kernel::os_directory::client::InstalledServiceContributionV1>) {\n    scenes::install_native_host_temporal_formatter(std::sync::Arc::new(native_temporal::SystemTemporalFormatter::default()));\n    let event_loop = EventLoop::<winit_app::HostUserEvent>::with_user_event().build().expect(\"event loop\");\n    let proxy = event_loop.create_proxy();\n    let mut app = winit_app::WinitApp::new(proxy, plugin_filter.to_string(), plugin_modules_root,services);\n    let _ = event_loop.run_app(&mut app);\n}\n\n/// 🧪️ ticket 26/08/17/FINISH-HUB-SPACES-COLLABORATION-END-TO-END — headless smoke mode: boots\n/// `ShellState` against a live hub (`S_HUB_URL`/`S_USER`/`S_DATA_DIR`) with NO GPU/window at all —\n/// `GpuContext`/`winit`/`AppRuntime` are the only GPU-coupled pieces in this crate and this mode never\n/// touches any of them, since `ShellState` itself is renderer-agnostic (chrome painting is a separate\n/// concern layered on top by `AppRuntime::frame`). Boots, waits (bounded) for identity to mint/restore\n/// and the initial directory fold to land, then dumps the Home window's widget tree + a small identity/\n/// session summary as JSON to stdout and returns an exit code. An honest, explicit substitute for\n/// driving a real window when this environment cannot open one (lane 3-D's brief proposed exactly this\n/// shape). Returns `0` on a clean boot+dump, `1` on any hard failure along the way.\n///\n/// 🪪️ Identity mint/restore runs on a background OS thread (contract §C3: never blocks\n/// `boot()` itself) — poll the same every-frame pump the real render loop uses (drains the\n/// identity bootstrap channel + the directory stream + folds any pending events) for up to 5s\n/// so a real hub round trip has time to land before the dump.\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))]\npub async fn run_smoke(plugin_filter: &str, plugin_modules_root: std::path::PathBuf,services:Vec<semio_framework_os_kernel::os_directory::client::InstalledServiceContributionV1>) -> i32 {\n    let loaded = match load_wasm_plugins(plugin_filter, &plugin_modules_root).await {\n        Ok(entries) => entries,\n        Err(error) => {\n            eprintln!(\"smoke: load_wasm_plugins failed: {error}\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    };\n    let entries = filter_plugins(loaded, plugin_filter);\n    let (locale, terminology) = match shell::shell_language_axes() {\n        Ok(axes) => axes,\n        Err(error) => { eprintln!(\"smoke: {error}\"); return 1; }\n    };\n    let mut shell = ShellState::new(entries, plugin_filter.to_string(), locale, terminology);\n    shell.install_document_services(services);\n    if let Err(error) = shell.boot().await {\n        eprintln!(\"smoke: shell.boot() failed: {error}\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n    let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);\n    while std::time::Instant::now() < deadline {\n        shell.pump_sync_events().await;\n        if shell.identity.is_some() || shell.identity_env.is_none() {\n            break;\n        }\n        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));\n    }\n    let _ = shell.refresh_ui(semio_framework::kernel::UiDirtyScope::Full).await;\n    let identity_summary = shell.identity.as_ref().map(|identity| serde_json::json!({ \"userId\": identity.user_id, \"email\": identity.email, \"hubBaseUrl\": identity.hub_base_url }));\n    let window_documents: Vec<_> = shell.window_ui.iter().map(|(window, document)| serde_json::json!({ \"window\": window, \"generation\": document.generation() })).collect();\n    let report = serde_json::json!({\n        \"booted\": true,\n        \"identity\": identity_summary,\n        \"identityOffline\": shell.identity_offline,\n        \"openSpaceId\": shell.open_space_id,\n        \"session\": shell.session.as_ref().map(|session| serde_json::json!({ \"pluginId\": session.plugin_id, \"appId\": session.app.id, \"role\": format!(\"{:?}\", session.app.role) })),\n        \"windowDocuments\": window_documents,\n    });\n    match serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) {\n        Ok(json) => {\n            println!(\"{json}\");\n            0\n        }\n        Err(error) => {\n            eprintln!(\"smoke: report encode failed: {error}\");\n            1\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🐚️ Multi-mount: takes an already-created, already-placed canvas from the caller instead of looking\n/// up a hardcoded `#root`/`#semio-wgpu-canvas` and taking it over via `set_inner_html(\"\")` — that\n/// single-mount assumption meant a second boot call would wipe the first mount's canvas and collide on\n/// the same DOM id. The caller (`bootFrameworkOsWgpu` in `🟦️.ts`) now owns creating and placing\n/// the canvas, so N independent mounts can coexist on one page.\n///\n/// Known gap (not yet done — see the plan's Wave 6 D11 notes), **narrowed but not closed** by ticket\n/// 26/08/20/SEMANTIC-UI-CONTRACT-AND-RENDERER-FAMILY (packet os-host): the independent, uncancellable\n/// `start_frame_loop`/`schedule_frame` recursive `requestAnimationFrame` chain this comment used to\n/// describe is DELETED — every redraw now goes through `winit`'s own event loop\n/// (`event_loop.spawn_app(app)` below → `winit_app::WinitApp`), and `WindowEvent::CloseRequested`\n/// already calls `ActiveEventLoop::exit()`. Whether `exit()` alone now fully tears down a wasm mount\n/// (winit's own wasm backend's post-`exit()` behaviour) is UNVERIFIED — this crate still does not\n/// build clean (U4, `📓️terra-os-host-report.md`), so a real `semioWgpuUnmount` handle remains\n/// deferred, but the mechanism it would need to cancel no longer exists in its old shape.\n/// The dozen-plus `thread_local!` globals further up this file (`UI_ENGINE`, `ENGINE_SURFACES`,\n/// `SCENE_STATE`, tooltip/dialog/tour chrome state, clipboard mocks, prefs, image-fetch caches, …) are\n/// also still page-global, not per-mount — two simultaneous wgpu mounts each render on their own\n/// independent GPU device/queue/surface (real, working isolation), but would still cross-talk on shared\n/// UI chrome auxiliary state (a tooltip or dialog opened in one mount could show in the other).\n#[cfg(target_arch = \"wasm32\")]\n#[wasm_bindgen(js_name = uploadIconAtlas)]\npub fn upload_icon_atlas(width: u32, height: u32, pixels: &[u8], entries_json: &str) -> Result<(), JsValue> {\n    let entries_map: std::collections::HashMap<String, [f32; 4]> = serde_json::from_str(entries_json).map_err(|err| JsValue::from_str(&format!(\"icon entries parse: {err}\")))?;\n    let entries: Vec<(String, [f32; 4])> = entries_map.into_iter().collect();\n    ICON_ATLAS_RUNTIME.with(|cell| {\n        cell.borrow_mut().replace(IconAtlas::from_packed(width, height, pixels.to_vec(), entries));\n    });\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nthread_local! {\n    static ICON_ATLAS_RUNTIME: RefCell<Option<IconAtlas>> = RefCell::new(None);\n}\n\n//#region 🧭️BootDescriptor\n// 🧭️ ONE boot-axis vocabulary for all three wgpu entry points — the trunk page\n// (`🚀️browser-boot/🟦️.ts`), the embeddable library door (`🎬️renderer-boot/🟦️.ts`) and the native CLI\n// (`⌨️native-entrypoint/🦀️.rs`) — and the Rust twin of `🧭️boot-descriptor/🟦️.ts`. React has a single\n// door (`FrameworkOsBootOptions`); wgpu had three, each carrying a different subset of the same axes,\n// so `--plugin cad --example concrete-forest` could not open natively what\n// `?plugin=cad&example=concrete-forest` opened in the browser. The standing law that keeps the four\n// field sets equal is `🧪️tests/🧭️boot-axis-parity/🦀️.rs`.\n//\n// Still a `thread_local` a caller opts into reading rather than a parameter threaded through every\n// mount signature: the shell reads it while it opens the session (`ShellState::boot`), which is why\n// every door applies it BEFORE mounting.\n\n/// 📏️ Bound on ONE descriptor field, the twin of `🧭️boot-descriptor/🟦️.ts`'s\n/// `WGPU_BOOT_FIELD_CAPACITY` — the browser door refuses an oversized url before it ever reaches\n/// here, and this is the same refusal for the native and library doors.\npub const WGPU_BOOT_FIELD_CAPACITY: usize = 2048;\n\n/// 🔒️ Boot-time preference LOCKS — React's `FrameworkOsLocks`. `\"\"` means unset, never \"locked to the\n/// empty string\"; a locked preference loses its in-app switcher.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"camelCase\", default)]\npub struct WgpuBootLocks {\n    pub example_id: String,\n    pub locale: String,\n    pub terminology: String,\n    pub theme_id: String,\n    pub appearance: String,\n}\n\n/// 🎛️ Boot-time preference DEFAULTS — React's `FrameworkOsDefaults`: seeds that KEEP their switcher.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"camelCase\", default)]\npub struct WgpuBootDefaults {\n    pub example_id: String,\n}\n\n/// 🏷️ The brand REGISTRY row this boot resolved — React's `resolveShellBrandById(brandId)` answer\n/// (`🧑‍💻dev/🏷️brand/🟦️.ts`), reduced to the facts the shell itself reads. The table stays where it is\n/// (a TypeScript catalogue over the demonstrator's own brand definitions); what crosses into the\n/// renderer is the resolved ROW, exactly as `locks`/`defaults` already do — so a brand added there\n/// needs no Rust edit and the two halves cannot drift into two catalogues.\n///\n/// `brand_id` alone was carried before this (`📓️w1d-boot-axis-parity.md` gap 1): the shell knew it was\n/// branded and nothing else, which is why the tour's persisted-seen key dropped React's brand prefix\n/// on every branded playground (`📓️w5a-browser-prefs-persistence.md` §7.1, demonstrated on\n/// `aggregator`).\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"camelCase\", default)]\npub struct WgpuBootBrand {\n    /// 🏷️ React's `ShellBrand.windowTitle` — the native window's title; `\"\"` leaves the default.\n    pub window_title: String,\n    /// 🧊️ React's `ShellBrand.ephemeral`: the shell never reads or writes device-local state.\n    pub ephemeral: bool,\n    /// 🎓️ React's `ShellBrand.replayIntroductionOnLoad` — auto-start every load, persist no seen flag.\n    /// `isEphemeralShellBrand` implies it there, and [`WgpuBootBrand::replays_introduction`] implies it\n    /// here, so the two predicates cannot disagree.\n    pub replay_introduction_on_load: bool,\n}\n\nimpl WgpuBootBrand {\n    /// 🎓️ React's `shouldReplayIntroductionOnLoad(brand)`.\n    pub fn replays_introduction(&self) -> bool {\n        self.ephemeral || self.replay_introduction_on_load\n    }\n\n    /// 🎓️ React's `shouldPersistIntroductionSeen(brand)`.\n    pub fn persists_introduction_seen(&self) -> bool {\n        !self.replays_introduction()\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌐️ The hub trio (`?hub=&user=&dataDir=`, `--hub/--user/--data-dir`).\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"camelCase\", default)]\npub struct WgpuBootHub {\n    pub hub_url: String,\n    pub user: String,\n    pub data_dir: String,\n}\n\n/// 🧭️ Every boot axis, resolved. Absent axes are `\"\"`/`Default` rather than `Option`, so the three\n/// doors cannot disagree about what \"unset\" serializes to.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"camelCase\", default)]\npub struct WgpuBootDescriptor {\n    pub plugin_variant: String,\n    pub app_id: String,\n    pub app_role: String,\n    pub app_mode: String,\n    pub app_example: String,\n    pub brand_id: String,\n    pub brand: WgpuBootBrand,\n    pub broker_proof: String,\n    pub locks: WgpuBootLocks,\n    pub defaults: WgpuBootDefaults,\n    pub hub: Option<WgpuBootHub>,\n}\n\nimpl WgpuBootDescriptor {\n    /// 📏️ Refuses an oversized field by NAME, so the fault says which axis overflowed — the Rust half\n    /// of `boundedBootField`. Applied before any axis is stored, never after.\n    pub fn validated(self) -> Result<Self, String> {\n        let hub = self.hub.as_ref();\n        let fields: [(&str, &str); 14] = [\n            (\"plugin\", self.plugin_variant.as_str()),\n            (\"app\", self.app_id.as_str()),\n            (\"role\", self.app_role.as_str()),\n            (\"mode\", self.app_mode.as_str()),\n            (\"example\", self.app_example.as_str()),\n            (\"brand\", self.brand_id.as_str()),\n            (\"brand.windowTitle\", self.brand.window_title.as_str()),\n            (\"brokerProof\", self.broker_proof.as_str()),\n            (\"locks.exampleId\", self.locks.example_id.as_str()),\n            (\"locks.locale\", self.locks.locale.as_str()),\n            (\"locks.terminology\", self.locks.terminology.as_str()),\n            (\"locks.themeId\", self.locks.theme_id.as_str()),\n            (\"locks.appearance\", self.locks.appearance.as_str()),\n            (\"defaults.exampleId\", self.defaults.example_id.as_str()),\n        ];\n        let hub_fields: [(&str, &str); 3] = [(\"hub\", hub.map_or(\"\", |hub| hub.hub_url.as_str())), (\"user\", hub.map_or(\"\", |hub| hub.user.as_str())), (\"dataDir\", hub.map_or(\"\", |hub| hub.data_dir.as_str()))];\n        for (field, value) in fields.into_iter().chain(hub_fields) {\n            if value.chars().count() > WGPU_BOOT_FIELD_CAPACITY {\n                return Err(format!(\"boot-descriptor-overflow: {field} exceeds {WGPU_BOOT_FIELD_CAPACITY} code units\"));\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(self)\n    }\n}\n\nthread_local! {\n    static BOOT_DESCRIPTOR: RefCell<WgpuBootDescriptor> = RefCell::new(resolve_environment_boot_descriptor());\n}\n\n/// 🖥️ The native per-server seeds, read straight off the process env under the SAME names React's\n/// serve projects into `VITE_SEMIO_*` (`🧑‍💻dev/🟦️.ts`). The CLI's own per-navigation flags overwrite\n/// these in `apply_boot_descriptor`; a browser build has no process env and starts empty.\n///\n/// 🏷️ The resolved brand ROW, under the same `SEMIO_*` names the serve injects as\n/// `<meta semio-brand-*>` for the browser door — one vocabulary, three doors.\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))]\nfn resolve_environment_boot_descriptor() -> WgpuBootDescriptor {\n    let read = |name: &str| std::env::var(name).ok().filter(|value| !value.is_empty()).unwrap_or_default();\n    WgpuBootDescriptor {\n        app_id: read(\"SEMIO_APP_ID\"),\n        app_role: read(\"SEMIO_APP_ROLE\"),\n        brand_id: read(\"SEMIO_BRAND\"),\n        brand: WgpuBootBrand { window_title: read(\"SEMIO_BRAND_WINDOW_TITLE\"), ephemeral: read(\"SEMIO_BRAND_EPHEMERAL\") == \"true\", replay_introduction_on_load: read(\"SEMIO_BRAND_REPLAY_INTRODUCTION\") == \"true\" },\n        app_example: read(\"SEMIO_DEFAULT_EXAMPLE\"),\n        defaults: WgpuBootDefaults { example_id: read(\"SEMIO_DEFAULT_EXAMPLE\") },\n        locks: WgpuBootLocks { example_id: read(\"SEMIO_LOCKED_EXAMPLE\"), locale: read(\"SEMIO_LOCKED_LOCALE\"), terminology: read(\"SEMIO_LOCKED_TERMINOLOGY\"), theme_id: read(\"SEMIO_LOCKED_THEME\"), appearance: read(\"SEMIO_LOCKED_APPEARANCE\") },\n        ..WgpuBootDescriptor::default()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(target_arch = \"wasm32\")]\nfn resolve_environment_boot_descriptor() -> WgpuBootDescriptor {\n    WgpuBootDescriptor::default()\n}\n\n/// 🧭️ Installs the resolved axes, replacing the environment seeds this thread started from. Every\n/// door calls it once, before the mount that opens the session.\npub fn apply_boot_descriptor(descriptor: WgpuBootDescriptor) -> Result<(), String> {\n    let descriptor = descriptor.validated()?;\n    BOOT_DESCRIPTOR.with(|cell| *cell.borrow_mut() = descriptor);\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// 🌐️ wasm boot hook — the frame Worker (`🎞️frame-worker/🟦️.ts`) and the page-mounted library door\n/// (`🎬️renderer-boot/🟦️.ts`) each call this once with the JSON `🧭️boot-descriptor/🟦️.ts` resolved.\n/// 🩺️ wasm diagnostics hook — the browser twin of the `SEMIO_RUNTIME_DIAGNOSTICS` environment\n/// variable a native process reads and of the `localStorage` key React's `ShellHost` reads. A Worker\n/// realm owns neither, so the UI isolate resolves the preference, stamps it on the frame Worker's url\n/// (`🎭️actor/🩺️diagnostics/🟦️.ts`'s `stampShardWorkerDiagnostics`) and the Worker hands it here —\n/// before the first frame, because every per-frame `[TRACE]` dump in this crate is gated on it.\n#[cfg(target_arch = \"wasm32\")]\n#[wasm_bindgen(js_name = semioWgpuSetRuntimeDiagnostics)]\npub fn semio_wgpu_set_runtime_diagnostics(enabled: bool) {\n    semio_framework_trace::set_runtime_diagnostics(enabled);\n}\n\n#[cfg(target_arch = \"wasm32\")]\n#[wasm_bindgen(js_name = semioWgpuSetBootDescriptor)]\npub fn semio_wgpu_set_boot_descriptor(descriptor_json: String) -> Result<(), JsValue> {\n    let descriptor: WgpuBootDescriptor = serde_json::from_str(&descriptor_json).map_err(|error| JsValue::from_str(&format!(\"boot-descriptor parse: {error}\")))?;\n    apply_boot_descriptor(descriptor).map_err(|error| JsValue::from_str(&error))\n}\n\n/// 🧭️ The whole resolved descriptor, for a reader that needs more than one axis.\npub fn boot_descriptor() -> WgpuBootDescriptor {\n    BOOT_DESCRIPTOR.with(|cell| cell.borrow().clone())\n}\n\nfn boot_axis(read: impl Fn(&WgpuBootDescriptor) -> &str) -> Option<String> {\n    BOOT_DESCRIPTOR.with(|cell| {\n        let descriptor = cell.borrow();\n        let value = read(&descriptor);\n        (!value.is_empty()).then(|| value.to_string())\n    })\n}\n\n/// 📌️ The boot-pinned app id, or `None`. React's `appId`: an empty value is NOT a pin, it falls\n/// through to the variant's own default app (`🧑‍💻dev/🟦️.ts`'s own note on `VITE_SEMIO_APP_ID`).\npub fn boot_app_id() -> Option<String> {\n    boot_axis(|descriptor| &descriptor.app_id)\n}\n\n/// 🎭️ The boot-requested mode id, or `None` when nothing named one. A mode the open app does not\n/// declare is ignored by the reader (`ShellState::apply_boot_mode`), never a boot failure.\npub fn boot_app_mode() -> Option<String> {\n    boot_axis(|descriptor| &descriptor.app_mode)\n}\n\n/// 📚️ The boot-requested example id, or `None`.
